Analyses of the X-ray surface brightness profiles of cluster cooling flows suggest that the mass flow rate decreases towards the center of the cluster.
The decrease in mass flow rate is often attributed to thermal instabilities, in which denser blobs of gas cool rapidly and drop below X-ray emitting temperatures.
If the seeds for the thermal instabilities are entropy perturbations, these perturbations must enter the flow already in the nonlinear regime, otherwise the blobs would take too long to cool.
The paper suggests that the nonlinear perturbations might start as blobs of interstellar gas which are stripped from cluster galaxies.

The total rate of gas stripping from galaxies is roughly that the typical rates of cooling in cluster cooling flows, suggesting that a substantial portion of the cooling flow material may be stripped from galaxies.
Magnetic fields within and outside the entropy perturbations can help maintain their identities, both by suppressing thermal conduction and through the dynamical effects of magnetic tension.

Cooling flows are only seen in a fraction of clusters, and the paper suggests this may be because the density perturbations only survive and cool efficiently in clusters with a very high intracluster gas density and with the focusing effect of a central dominant galaxy.
The density fluctuations caused by gas stripping may disrupt the propagation of radio jets through the intracluster gas, which may be one mechanism for producing Wide-Angle-Tail radio galaxies.
